request.title: Refute two printed claims of §9.2.2 (Ch09 Sec2_Printed: #5815, #5816)
request.body:
Proves both refutations in `RiemannMasullo/Ch09_HardySobolev/Sec2_Printed.lean` (ERRATA F233, F237). No statement changed; only proofs and `private theorem` helpers placed above the first refutation.

Closes #5815
Closes #5816

**Counterexample used** (different from the bump/Mellin family sketched in the docstrings, simpler to formalize): the tilted Gaussians `u_m(z) = exp(m(z − 1) + z²)`, m ∈ ℕ, which lie in `SchwartzBergman univ`. On the line Re z = σ the L² norm of `u_m` is `exp(m(σ − 1))` times that of the Gaussian, so it tends to 0 when σ < 1 and is constant when σ = 1, while `u_m(1) = e` for every m. Abscissas `c n = (−1)ⁿ (1 − 1/(n+2))` accumulate at both ends of [−1, 1] and all lie below 1.

- `Printed.sampledHardySobolevTopology_independent_false` (Proposition 9.2.2.4(1), p. 414): with s = 0, `u_m → 0` in the topology sampled on `c`, but not in the topology sampled on `d` (= `c` with the line at 1 prepended), since the order-zero ball on the line Re z = 1 of radius ‖Gaussian‖ excludes every `u_m`. So the two topologies differ.
- `Printed.sampledHardySobolev_eval_boundary_iff_false` (Corollary 9.2.2.5(2), p. 414): with s = 1, z = 1, k = 0 the printed floor allows k = 0, but evaluation at 1 is not continuous: `u_m → 0` in the sampled topology while `u_m(1) = e`.

Helpers (all `private theorem`): membership of the tilted Gaussians, their line norms, finiteness/nonvanishing of the Gaussian line norm, convergence of `u_m` to 0 in the sampled topology (order zero, abscissas < 1), and the bounds/clustering of the abscissas.
